body.x: Aldaver (CEOs Jin-oh Kim & Steve Park) participated in the 'Startup Zone' at the Eureka Park K-STARTUP integrated hall of 'CES 2023' in Las Vegas, USA from January 5 (Thursday) to 8 (Sunday, local time) for a total of 4 days.

Aldaver has developed products that enable surgeons to practice robotic surgery in a very realistic manner. This is done by using carcasses and synthetic organs made with 3D printing technology based on biopolymer materials, which have important properties in emulating actual surgery. The company has proven its innovation and excellence by winning several startup competitions.

In this exhibition, Aldaver introduced a skin suture model. The strong points include the realistic touch and implementation of the physical properties of all layers of skin. In addition, product customizations are available depending on the layer thickness and physical properties.

According to a representative from Aldaver, "The silicon-based surgical training simulators on the market are not quite like the real thing in terms of touch and physical properties. This makes the training more difficult. Simulators on pigs provide a good sense of realism, but there are restrictions due to legal regulations in regard to ethical issues.” They added, “We wanted to improve the surgical environment for medical staff by developing a new material-based surgical simulator that mimics the physical properties of the real human body.”
Not needing to worry about ethical issues and legal regulations liberates healthcare service providers to take surgical training anytime and anywhere, improving their expertise.

“In CES, we intend to have interviews on several surgical robotic makers and introduce our technology,” said the representative in describing the reason for their participation. They added, “Our aim is to cooperate with various surgical robotic enterprises to develop synthetic products that meet their needs. Specifications vary from business to business, but materials can be quickly adjusted to meet the specifications with the technology that's already been developed.”

‘CES’ is the world’s biggest IT trade show and is a place where one can see the direction and trends of the appliance industry of the entire world. Hosted by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), it is held annually in Las Vegas, USA in January. Having reported on CES for 17 consecutive years, AVING News started reporting news of CES to the entire world since 2006, and conducted ‘BEST OF CES’, which chose the most innovative product and technology, and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA, which chose the best innovative company in Korea. In addition, it vividly relayed on-site issues in CES through ‘AVING LIVE’.

The K-STARTUP Joint Pavilion featured joint participation of institutions like the Korea Institute of Startup & Entrepreneurship Development, Seoul Business Agency, and Seoul Digital Foundation, as well as 51 Korean innovative companies, to enter the US market and discover global partners. In addition, university student supporters of CES 2023 chosen by each university (Kyunghee, Kookmin, Sogang, Chung-Ang) matched to participating companies based on their respective majors and fields of business.
